Article Title: 5 poll-bound states set to vote in February-March
Article Text:
5 poll bound states to vote in Feb-March

UP will vote almost 2 months before House term expires

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The advancement of Census in the four poll-bound states of Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Punjab and Goa - coupled with deferment of first phase of Census in the fifth poll-bound state of Manipur - has essentially cemented the schedule for the next round of assembly elections in the five states to Feb-March next year.Among the five states, the term of the Manipur assembly is expiring the earliest - on March 13, 2027. The term of Goa assembly ends March 14, 2027; Punjab assembly on March 16; Uttarakhand on March 28; and Uttar Pradesh only on May 22. All five had gone to polls together in 2022, but the first sitting of the UP assembly was on May 22, 2022.Since 2027 polls in these states will also be simultaneous, Election Commission is likely to take the conventional route of winding up polls before the earliest assembly expiry date - March 13.Thus, the UP polls would be held almost two months before the date of expiry of its assembly. This is in keeping with the pattern of the last three polls. EC's constitutional mandate allows it to hold a state poll anytime within six months prior to the expiry of its assembly's term.Given that a large and populous state like UP is almost certain to have multi-phase polling - though with fewer phases, going by the precedent set by EC in Bihar and West Bengal - polling could start in Feb or even in the beginning of March in case EC decides to restrict polls to two phases, like in Bihar.The poll announcement may come in Jan 2027.Since SIR has already been completed in three poll-bound states and is under way in the other two, EC is unlikely to go for annual summary revision there ahead of announcing assembly polls. At the end of SIR, the electorate in UP stood at 13.4 crore (decline of 13.2%), in Goa 10.6 lakh (10.2% less) and in Manipur 19.3 lakh (7.6% fall). The final rolls for Punjab and Uttarakhand will be published over the next couple of months.Centre had yesterday notified its decision to advance the population enumeration phase of Census 2027 in Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, non-snow-bound areas of Uttarakhand and Goa, to the period between Dec 1, 2026, and Jan 4, 2027, with Jan 5 as the reference date. It also notified the deferment of the houselisting phase of Census in Manipur.The advancing of the population enumeration phase in the four other poll-bound states will avert the logistical challenges that would have arisen on account of a clash between the usual timeline for Census and the assembly elections. Both elections and Census rely on the same pool of govt employees - largely teachers - for their conduct.Conventionally, the second phase of Census is held countrywide in Feb, with March 1 as the reference date.
Article Summary: The term of the Manipur assembly is expiring the earliest - on March 13, 2027. Election Commission is likely to take the conventional route of winding up polls before the earliest assembly expiry date. All five had gone to polls together in 2022, but the first sitting of the UP assembly was on May 22, 2022.

NEW DELHI: BJP and Congress chiefs Sunday sparred over PM Narendra Modi's 'naraaz fufa' (disgruntled uncle) jibe at opponents and critics, with Mallikarjun Kharge questioning the PM's use of such labels and Nitin Nabin responding that his counterpart's criticism was yet another confirmation of his party's negative mindset.In a post on X in Hindi, Kharge said, "Modi ji's modus operandi is to suppress questions in a democracy and give the opposition a new adjective every year so that his own failures remain hidden! Naraaz fufa, dimagi Naxal, urban Naxal, Khan Market gang, andolan-jeevi, parjeevi..." The adjectives for the opposition may keep changing, but Modi govt's "anti-people policies" do not change, Kharge added.He asked the govt to listen to 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' as solutions won't come from beating around the bush.In response to this, Nabin justified the PM's colloquial jibe saying the opposition has indeed been acting like that one uncle in the family who always sulks and can never see or appreciate good things. "There are some people who remain dissatisfied within the family and the society and can never think positively. It was precisely this set that the PM referred to when he said 'naraaz fufa'," Nabin said.The BJP president said that the opposition has not appreciated Modi govt's success in tackling terrorism or in bringing more than 25 crore people out of poverty. "I want to know why they get angry when Modi govt scraps special status for J&K, controls terrorism, or eliminates Maoism." They promised to abolish poverty but failed. But why should they get angry when Modi govt has realised what was promised by them? he asked.Nabin accused Kharge of failing to see the reality of things because "you are totally immersed in pursuing your own selfish interests".
Article Summary: BJP and Congress chiefs Sunday sparred over PM Narendra Modi's 'naraaz fufa' (disgruntled uncle) jibe at opponents and critics. Mallikarjun Kharge questioned the PM's use of such labels and Nitin Nabin responded that his counterpart's criticism was yet another confirmation of his party's negative mindset.

Article Title: 'Contributed to population control': Former CEC Quraishi says EC 'eliminated' 15 cr voters through SIR
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Former Chief Election Commissioner SY Quraishi on Sunday criticised the Election Commission over its special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, claiming that the exercise had effectively removed around 14-15 crore people from the country's voter lists.Speaking to news agency ANI, Quraishi urged the poll panel to disclose the number of voters deleted, describing the exercise as a "great success" in achieving something the National Population Commission could not."I would like to compliment the Election Commission for completing a very difficult mission of eliminating about 14-15 crore population of India through this exercise. I don't know how many illegal immigrants they have found, which was the main purpose of this exercise. It's a pity they have not disclosed this figure," Quraishi said."I would request them to please come out with this figure, so that we know what a great success you have been, and also that you have achieved something that the National Population Commission could not do. You have contributed a lot to population control by eliminating about 15% of India's population," he added.Quraishi also questioned the intent behind the SIR exercise, arguing that voting is a constitutional right and not something to be granted by the Election Commission."I think the entire SIR exercise is not well-intentioned. The way it has deleted crores of voters is tinkering with democracy. You are a citizen of India. I'm a citizen of India. Voting is our constitutional right," he said."Article 326 says that everyone shall be registered. So it is not a charity from the Election Commission that they will give you that," he added.The Election Commission is conducting the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls in several states to ensure that voter lists are accurate, updated and free of ineligible or duplicate entries, while ensuring that no eligible voter is left out.The nationwide SIR was announced in October 2025 by Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The poll panel cited migration, voters being registered at multiple places, failure to remove deceased voters and the inclusion of foreign nationals in electoral rolls as factors behind the exercise.The revision has since been rolled out across several states and Union territories, including those heading into elections. The exercise has drawn sustained criticism from opposition parties.In Maharashtra, the SIR came under scrutiny after the draft electoral roll showed around two crore fewer voters than the previous roll.According to data released by Maharashtra's Chief Electoral Officer, 7,71,65,562 of the state's 9,78,54,049 electors had submitted their enumeration forms as of August 17.
Article Summary: Former Chief Election Commissioner SY Quraishi criticises the Election Commission over its special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. He claims that the exercise had effectively removed around 14-15 crore people from the country's voter lists. Qurasishi also questioned the intent behind the SIR exercise, arguing that voting is a constitutional right.

Article Title: ‘Scared to work’: Ex-Pakistan cricketer opens up on Mohsin Naqvi-led PCB
Article Text:
Chairman of Pakistan Cricket Board Mohsin Naqvi, centre, chats with Pakistan's Babar Azam, left, as head coach Mike Hesson watches (AP Photo)

Mushtaq reveals why he is hesitant

'This is not the right thing'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

PCB under growing scrutiny

The Pakistan Cricket Board’s decision to overhaul the national team in the middle of its England tour continues to face scrutiny, with former Pakistan spinner Mushtaq Ahmed admitting that the uncertainty surrounding coaching positions has made him wary of taking up a role with the national side.A week after the PCB sent seven players and two coaches back to Pakistan, the fallout from the decision remains a major talking point. The board has frequently faced criticism for making repeated changes to its coaches and captains, and Mushtaq believes that the lack of stability is now becoming a deterrent for former players who want to serve Pakistan in coaching roles.The PCB took the drastic step after Pakistan suffered heavy defeats in the opening two Tests against England. Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq and Salman Ali Agha were among the players sent home, while Sarfaraz Ahmed and Umar Gul were also removed from the coaching setup. They were replaced in the dressing room by Mike Hesson and Ashley Noffke.Mushtaq was asked whether he would be interested in coaching Pakistan and made it clear that he would welcome the chance to work with the national team. However, he also explained why the current environment leaves him concerned about accepting such a responsibility.The former spinner pointed to the treatment of coaches and the possibility of being removed abruptly, even while a tour is still in progress.“I would love to do that for my country, of course. Especially at this time.Obviously, I need only one thing. Sometimes you get scared of working for your own country when the people don’t respect you, and they sack you because of a few emotional decisions here and there. When you see those things, people getting sacked on a tour, you get worried and scared,” Mushtaq said on the BBC Stumped Podcast.Despite his concerns, Mushtaq believes there is an opportunity for Pakistani coaches to make a meaningful contribution if greater stability can be established within the system.“I think those are the things that if you can get that sorted, I think every Pakistani cricketer who is coaching, not only myself, they’d love to serve the country. This is the best time for me to take that challenge and bring those players to their best, make them confident about international cricket and make a unit that can actually challenge opposition teams,” he added.Mushtaq also strongly disagreed with the PCB's decision to make such sweeping changes while the England series was still underway.The former Pakistan international, who played 52 Tests and 144 ODIs, questioned the rationale behind sending seven players home and altering the coaching staff midway through an overseas tour.“Changing seven players and the management, especially with the tour still going on, I feel that this is not the right thing,” Mushtaq said.He was particularly critical of the timing of the decision involving Sarfaraz and Umar Gul, arguing that changes of this magnitude should have been considered after the completion of the tour.“This has never happened in Pakistan cricket before. Obviously, I’m hurt as an ex-cricketer, as a Pakistani, these things should not happen. Sarfaraz and Umar Gul, they are some of the most experienced cricketers. They serve the country very well. Sarfaraz was a captain also. If you want to sack them, obviously, you have to sack them after the tour. This is the time to stay calm, don’t make rash decisions," he added.The mid-tour shake-up has attracted criticism beyond Pakistan, with Michael Atherton, Nasser Hussain and Jason Gillespie among those who have questioned the PCB's decision.The board's changes came after Pakistan's disappointing results in the first two Tests, leaving the team facing the prospect of a difficult end to the tour.Pakistan will now look to finish the series on a positive note when they face England in the third and final Test, beginning on September 9 in Birmingham. However, with questions over the board's approach to coaches, players and decision-making continuing to mount, the debate surrounding Pakistan cricket is unlikely to end with the conclusion of the Test series.
Article Summary: Mushtaq Ahmed reveals why he is hesitant to take up a coaching role with the Pakistan national side. The former spinner believes that the uncertainty surrounding coaching positions has made him wary of taking up a role. Mushtaq also questioned the rationale behind sending seven players home and altering the coaching staff midway through an overseas tour. He was particularly critical of the timing of the decision involving Sarfaraz and Umar Gul.

Article Title: Who was Bill Dundee? Wrestling legend and Jerry "The King" Lawler’s longtime friend passes away at 82
Article Text:
Bill Dundee. Image via: Memphis Wrestling/ YouTube

Who was Bill Dundee?

Bill Dundee dies at 82, family and WWE react

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Bill Dundee's wrestling legacy

Bill Dundee spent more than half a century inside wrestling rings across three continents, and somehow his final on-camera moment landed just one day before his death. That kind of timing doesn't happen by design, but it's exactly how Memphis wrestling said goodbye to one of its own.Dundee died early Sunday morning at 82. His son, Jamie Dundee, broke the news, and within hours tributes started pouring in from a wrestling world that had watched Dundee build his legacy over five decades.Bill Dundee was born William Cruickshanks in Scotland and grew up in Australia, where his path into wrestling started in an unlikely place. As a teenager, he joined a circus and worked as a trapeze artist before ever stepping into a ring. He began wrestling professionally in Australia in the late 1960s and arrived in the United States in 1974.Memphis became his home base, and his career there became inseparable from Jerry "The King" Lawler. The two spent years shifting between fierce rivals and championship-winning partners, and their matches, built around elaborate stipulations and personal feuds, turned into some of the most memorable moments in Memphis wrestling history.Dundee also worked behind the scenes as a booker in several territories, a role that shaped the business as much as his in-ring work did.Jamie Dundee announced his father's death on Facebook early Sunday, saying he died at around 3:30 a.m. and signing off, "Bill's Boy." No cause of death has been made public. Jamie had previously revealed that his father was living with stage three dementia, though nothing has tied that diagnosis to his death.WWE released a statement Sunday afternoon, writing that it was "saddened to learn that Memphis wrestling legend Bill Dundee has passed away," and extended condolences to his family and fans.Just a day earlier, Memphis Wrestling aired what turned out to be Dundee's final televised appearance, recorded before it aired Saturday on WMC. Current roster members lined up to shake his hand as announcer Dustin Starr recalled his championship battles with Lawler.Nobody watching knew it would double as a farewell.Dundee held the AWA Southern Heavyweight Championship nine times and the CWA International Heavyweight Championship four times, and alongside Lawler, he won the AWA World Tag Team Championship twice, including a run that began in October 1987. Their most famous feud, in 1977, carried hair stipulations and even Lawler's Cadillac as a wager.He was inducted into the Memphis Wrestling Hall of Fame in 2017, sharing the stage with Lawler, Jimmy Hart, and Koko B. Ware. Dundee kept wrestling well past his prime years, taking his final match in December 2019, nearly 45 years after he first landed in Memphis. He also spent time in WCW under the name Sir William, managing Steven Regal.
Article Summary: Bill Dundee died early Sunday morning at 82. His son, Jamie Dundee, announced the news on Facebook. Dundee was inducted into the Memphis Wrestling Hall of Fame in 2017. He spent more than half a century wrestling across three continents.

Article Title: Trophy controversy returns? Mohsin Naqvi set to attend India’s Women’s Asia Cup final
Article Text:
Indian Men's Cricket Team and Mohsin Naqvi

Trophy drama could return

What happened in last year's final?

Why would Naqvi present the trophy?

India dominate Women's Asia Cup campaign

Yes, it’s about sportsmanship No, due to past controversies Only if there are assurances of goodwill It doesn't matter, win is what counts 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

The possibility of another trophy presentation controversy involving India and Pakistan has emerged ahead of the ACC Women’s Asia Cup 2026 final, with Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) chairman and Asian Cricket Council (ACC) president Mohsin Naqvi set to attend the summit clash in Dubai.According to a Geo Super report, Naqvi is expected to be the chief guest at the closing ceremony of the tournament on September 13. His presence could once again bring the focus on the trophy presentation if Harmanpreet Kaur’s India reach the final and go on to win the title.Naqvi was at the centre of a major controversy during last year's Men's Asia Cup final at the Dubai International Stadium. India defeated Pakistan in the summit clash but refused to accept the trophy from Naqvi, who was the ACC president and also PCB chairman.The episode took place against a particularly tense backdrop. The Men's Asia Cup was played after the Pahalgam terror attack, while Naqvi had also shared anti-India statements on social media during the tournament in his capacity as Pakistan's Interior Minister.With Naqvi expected to attend the Women's Asia Cup final, another trophy-related standoff could potentially unfold.If India win the tournament, Naqvi could be the official presenting the silverware to the champions because of his position as ACC president.The decision on whether to accept it from him, however, would ultimately rest with the Harmanpreet-led Indian team.The BCCI has so far remained silent on what the women's side would do if they win the tournament and Naqvi is present for the presentation.India are among the favourites for the title and have already secured their place in the semi-finals without losing a match. They made a particularly strong statement against Pakistan, defeating the Fatima Sana-led side by seven wickets after bowling them out for just 55 in Dubai.The controversy involving Naqvi began after India defeated Pakistan in the Men's Asia Cup final on September 28, 2025.The Suryakumar Yadav-led Indian side completed the victory, but the post-match presentation was delayed by more than an hour as discussions continued over who would present the trophy.India eventually chose not to receive the silverware from Naqvi. The players celebrated their title triumph on the podium without the trophy, while Naqvi left the stadium with it.The Asia Cup trophy has still not been handed over to India and remains at the ACC office in Dubai.The situation became one of the most talked-about moments of the tournament, particularly because Naqvi had attended the final despite the earlier tensions between the two sides.Naqvi holds two key positions relevant to the presentation. He is the PCB chairman as well as the president of the ACC.Since the Women's Asia Cup is an ACC-hosted tournament, Naqvi, by virtue of his position as ACC president, holds the right to present the trophy to the winners.That means another India-Pakistan trophy moment could be waiting in Dubai if Harmanpreet Kaur's team reaches the final and lifts the title.India have been unbeaten throughout their campaign in the eight-team Women's Asia Cup. Harmanpreet Kaur's side began the tournament with a victory over Thailand before producing convincing wins against Hong Kong and Pakistan in the group stage.The tournament has also witnessed a major individual milestone for Smriti Mandhana, who became the leading run-scorer in women's international cricket after surpassing former India captain Mithali Raj.With India already through to the semi-finals, attention will now turn to the knockout stage. If the Women in Blue make it all the way to the final and win the trophy on September 13, Naqvi's presence could set the stage for another closely watched presentation ceremony in Dubai.
Article Summary: Mohsin Naqvi set to attend ACC Women's Asia Cup 2026 final. Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) chairman and Asian Cricket Council (ACC) president is expected to be the chief guest at the closing ceremony in Dubai. If India win the tournament, he could be the official presenting the silverware to the champions because of his position as ACC president. The decision on whether to accept it from him would ultimately rest with the Harmanpreet-led Indian team.

Article Title: ‘Men would never have to face this’: Keyaa Banerji calls out sexism after viral 140kg deadlift and World Championship silver
Article Text:
21-year-old Keyaa Banerji (Image Source: X)

ALSO READ:

A medal, a viral lift and an uncomfortable spotlight

‘I was aiming to break the Asian record’

‘It’s always something I really enjoyed’

More than just lifting heavy weights

Looking beyond the online noise

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Indian powerlifter Keyaa Kunal Banerji had every reason to expect attention after producing one of the standout performances of her young career. Instead, the 21-year-old found herself confronting an uncomfortable side of online fame after her 140kg deadlift and World Championship silver medal went viral.Banerji's breakthrough came at the 2026 IPF World Sub-Junior and Junior Classic Powerlifting Championships in Sun City, South Africa, where she competed in the Junior Women's 47kg category. Weighing 45.70kg, she pulled 140kg in the deadlift — more than three times her competition bodyweight — to finish second in the individual deadlift event and win a silver medal.But as the clip of her lift spread across social media, much of the conversation around her achievement shifted away from powerlifting. Banerji said she was subjected to trolling, fake accounts, misuse of her images and thousands of unauthorised AI-generated manipulated images using her likeness.For the young athlete, the experience was not simply about unpleasant comments. She saw it as a stark example of the sexism women athletes continue to encounter when their achievements attract a large online audience."I think it was just sexism at its finest. I don't think I can put it any other way.The way I was treated - men would never have to face this, like after winning a championship or something like that; a male athlete never has to face something like this," Banerji told ANI."Most of the conversation revolved around my appearance. All people would talk about was my appearance, and I think that really bothered me because I had accomplished something so big for myself and I had done something so big in my sport," she added.The irony was not lost on Banerji. The lift that drew widespread attention was itself the product of years of work and a sport that she has come to deeply enjoy.At the World Championships, Banerji also recorded a 90kg squat and a 50kg bench press, finishing with a 280kg total and placing fifth overall in the Junior Women's 47kg category. France's Ines Herbaux won the individual deadlift gold with 165kg, while Ireland's Blathnaid O'Dwyer also lifted 140kg.Banerji, however, had arrived at the competition with ambitions that went beyond simply making the podium."I think initially it is a great feeling. Once it came out on social media, I did get a little bit overwhelmed. There was some negative attention, but I would like to avoid talking about that too much. I am very proud of myself and very happy with my accomplishment. I have been working towards this for two years," she said.The silver medal itself had not been part of her original expectations."This silver medal was something I wasn't expecting initially. I was just happy to be present at the World Championship because powerlifting is a long-term sport. I do have plans of eventually winning a World Championship and getting a gold back for the country," Banerji said."It started with me thinking that this World Championship is something I'm going to attend just for experience. The fact that I ended up putting such a good number up and winning a medal was just absolutely incredible," she added.The 140kg deadlift became the defining moment of her campaign, but Banerji's own assessment of the lift was more measured. She explained that competition-day performances can differ considerably from what an athlete manages in training."Competition day numbers and training numbers aren't always the same. Performing as an athlete on competition day is very different from what you do in training. In powerlifting, we usually try to hit maxes in competition," she said."Although my result worked out in a way that I won a silver medal, as an athlete, the planning that my coach and I had done, 140 kg was on the lower end of the range for what we were planning to hit that day," she added.In training, Banerji had already gone beyond that mark."In training, I have hit around 147.5 kg and 150 kg several times. 147.5 kg is also the Asian record. So, my ideal day would have been breaking the Asian record on stage. I was a little disheartened that I wasn't able to do that," she said.The 140kg lift was only her second deadlift attempt. She subsequently went for 142.5kg but could not complete it."140 kg wasn't my third deadlift; it was my second deadlift. It moved a little bit slower than expected compared to how it moves in training. So, I took a smaller jump of 142.5 after that, and I failed that lift. It wasn't an ideal day, but things worked out," she said.While the online attention was difficult, Banerji does not want the trolling to define the story of her World Championship campaign."In fact, I'm really grateful for the opportunity to be talking to news channels because it gives me the opportunity to actually talk about my passion for the sport and my journey progressing my numbers, etc. So, I'm over it. I'm definitely over it. But it was a little bit hard in the middle," she said.That passion dates back to when powerlifting was not even part of her plans."When I was first starting out, I just started going to the gym for a sense of personal fulfilment and just taking care of my health, etc. But I had a friend who was a powerlifting coach and was also competing at a world level. He has also won a gold medal for the country. So, I felt extremely inspired and felt very curious about how this works," she said.That curiosity eventually became competitive ambition as her numbers improved in the squat, bench press and deadlift.Banerji also stressed that powerlifting is a highly technical discipline, contrary to the simplistic perception that it is merely about lifting as much weight as possible."There are rules, making sure that your lift matches the commands of the referee, making sure that once you've picked up, for instance, once you've completed your deadlift, you can't just leave the bar. You can only put it down once the referee asks you to put it down. So, there are a lot of, it's a very technical sport. There are a lot of things that go into it," she said.For Banerji, the sport has also been a constant through an important period of her life."My sport is something that really helped me in my life. During my college times, I used to look forward to training. Sometimes I would have to train at night, sometimes I would have to skip classes to train, but it's something that never really bothered me. It's always something I really enjoyed," she said.Her progression is reflected in her numbers. At the 2025 National Championship, she lifted 82.5kg in the squat, 47.5kg in the bench press and 127.5kg in the deadlift for a 257.5kg total. She later improved to 95kg in the squat, 52.5kg in the bench press and 140kg in the deadlift, taking her total to 287.5kg.The World Championship therefore represented another significant step, even if her own assessment suggests there is considerably more to come."I can't explain it, and I am overwhelmed. I was very happy to just be there. To be at that World Championship, meet my competitors, see the girls that I used to look up to around me and compete in the same competition — it was an unreal feeling," she said.Banerji, who recently graduated from Ashoka University with a BSc in Psychology, is considering pursuing an MBA. But her immediate sporting ambition remains clear: continue improving her numbers and eventually win a World Championship gold for India.The unwanted online attention may have become part of her story, but it is not what Banerji wants to be remembered for.
Article Summary: Keyaa Kunal Banerji, 21, won a silver medal at the 2026 IPF World Sub-Junior and Junior Classic Powerlifting Championships in South Africa. She pulled 140kg in the deadlift, more than three times her competition bodyweight. But as the clip of her lift spread across social media, much of the conversation around her achievement shifted away from powerlifting. She said she was subjected to trolling, fake accounts, misuse of her images and thousands of unauthorised AI- generated manipulated images.

Article Title: Bengaluru techie dies after speeding BMW RR sports bike hits car
Article Text:
A software engineer died and his friend was injured after a speeding BMW bike hit their car.





BENGALURU: A 25-year-old software engineer was killed and another person was injured after a BMW RR sports bike rammed into their Swift Dzire car near Chikkasanne Gate on NH-44 late Saturday night.The deceased has been identified as Naveen Gowda N, a resident of Neraganahalli village in Devanahalli taluk. His 26-year-old friend Avinash, who was travelling in the same car, suffered injuries and is undergoing treatment at a private hospital.According to the complaint filed by Ashok, 29, the group of friends were returning from a dhaba near Devanahalli after a dinner party in the car that one of them, Manas Gowda, borrowed from his friend.Manas was driving the car and, around 11.50 pm, as the vehicle was taking a turn towards Chikkasanne village, the BMW RR bike came at high speed and crashed into the front-left door of the car.The impact left the car badly damaged. Naveen, who was seated beside the driver, suffered fatal injuries to his head and body, while Avinash, who was sitting in the rear seat, sustained an injury near his left eye.The biker, identified as Rakesh Chaudhary, was thrown onto the road along with the bike, and suffered injuries.The bike was also heavily damaged.Naveen and Avinash were shifted to a private hospital in Devanahalli around 12.30am where doctors declared Naveen dead.Avinash was later shifted to another hospital at Kodigehalli Junction for further treatment.A senior police officer further said, "Soon after the incident came to our notice, a team rushed to the spot. Both the vehicles were seized, and the injured were taken to hospital by then. The accused Rakesh got discharged from the hospital and is at large. We didn't get the MLC report from any hospital about him. We have learnt that he is a resident of Rajanukunte and a native of Gurgaon, Haryana. Once apprehended, we will know if he was riding under the influence of alcohol. "A case has been registered at Devanahalli traffic police station against the bike rider for overspeeding and negligent riding, causing a death.
Article Summary: A BMW RR sports bike rammed into a Swift Dzire car near Chikkasanne Gate on NH-44 late Saturday night. Article Title: ‘This is not sustainable’: US Open’s post-2 am finishes spark player backlash as Navratilova, Becker question late-night scheduling
Article Text:
Matches increasingly spill into the early hours at US Open 2026. (Pic credit: X/AP)

‘Everybody wants to go to sleep’

Alexander Zverev of Germany (AP Photo)

Pegula questions whether it is ‘the right thing’

Jessica Pegula of the United States (AP Photo)

Venus Williams caught in historic late start

Shelton experiences his first 2 am finish

Aryna Sabalenka of Belarus (AP Photo)

Sabalenka warns of disrupted schedules

The US Open’s famous late-night energy is once again coming under scrutiny, but this time the concern is not about whether New York can keep the party going. It is about whether the players can.As the first week of the Grand Slam winds down, a growing number of matches have stretched well past midnight, with three of the first six night sessions finishing after 2 am (local time) and two others extending beyond 1 am. The unusually late endings have prompted four-time US Open singles champion Martina Navratilova , six-time Grand Slam winner Boris Becker and several players to question whether the scheduling has gone too far.Navratilova was among the most direct in her criticism, posting on X after the tournament recorded three post-2 am finishes in its opening six days."This is not sustainable…": Navratilova wrote while sharing statistics highlighting the late finishes.Becker, the 1989 US Open champion, also weighed in after Navratilova's post, questioning why tennis players are being asked to compete at such hours."That’s simple to late to play tennis ?? anymore….tell me another sport like that ?!?," Becker posted.The issue has become particularly noticeable in a tournament where night tennis has long been part of its identity.Arthur Ashe Stadium under the lights, packed stands and an electric New York crowd are among the defining images of the US Open. But as matches increasingly spill into the early hours, players and former champions are beginning to question where the line should be drawn.Alexander Zverev had little appetite for an extended discussion after his first-round match ended in the early hours. With empty seats visible around the court, the German top seed took just two questions from reporters before making his feelings clear."I think everybody's tired," he said. "Everybody wants to go to sleep."The problem became even more pronounced for Zverev as the tournament progressed. His first two matches finished at 1:55 am and 2:15 am, respectively, making him the first top-seeded man to play back-to-back five-set matches to begin a major in the Open era, which dates back to 1968.His experience has underlined the physical cost of the scheduling, particularly when players have to recover from long matches and then prepare for the next round within a limited window.Third-ranked women's player Jessica Pegula acknowledged that tournament organisers have to balance several competing demands, including television schedules and match timings. But she questioned whether those considerations should come at the expense of players having to compete deep into the night."I know they're dealing with a lot of different aspects as far as broadcast and TV and making sure certain matches get done and are starting at a certain time for those reasons," Pegula said."But you have to wonder if it's really the right thing for players to be finishing at 2 am, especially when it’s not — like, I'm not watching on TV. I'm sleeping. Some people stay, but there is a lot of people that need to go home."Her comments reflect a broader concern around the sustainability of the current schedule. A late finish does not simply mean a player leaves the court later. It can affect meals, recovery, sleep and preparation for the following day.Other Grand Slam tournaments have taken different approaches. Wimbledon has instituted an 11 pm curfew, while the French Open schedules only one match during its night session.The US Open, meanwhile, has traditionally embraced the possibility of matches running deep into the night. This year's schedule, however, has pushed that tradition to an extreme.The issue was apparent from the opening night itself.Novak Djokovic's first-round match lasted four hours and 36 minutes on August 30. The length of that contest pushed Venus Williams and Sofia Kenin onto court at 12:13 am, the latest match start in US Open history.Much of the crowd stayed to watch what could have been the 46-year-old Williams' final Grand Slam singles match. But the timing made the occasion more difficult for both players."It's not ideal," Williams said. "I would have preferred something else, definitely. It wasn't great for either of us, so I think we both tried our best. I just don't know any other sport where you have to start that late. I definitely think there's room for improvement there."The match eventually concluded at 2:01 am, adding another chapter to a tournament already seeing an unusual number of after-midnight finishes.Ben Shelton also found himself dealing with the consequences of the scheduling when his second-round match against Denis Shapovalov, which began on Friday night, finished at 2:07 am Saturday.The delay was partly caused by the Williams sisters' doubles match, which lasted more than three hours."Not easy," Shelton said after defeating Shapovalov in 3 hours, 22 minutes. "My first time experiencing playing this late."Shelton estimated that he would not get to sleep until around 5 am, highlighting how a match that ends after 2 am can effectively consume much of the following morning as well.Four of the 17 latest finishes in US Open history have now occurred this year. The tournament record remains 2:50 am, set in 2022 when Carlos Alcaraz defeated Jannik Sinner in the quarterfinals on his way to his first US Open title.Top-ranked Aryna Sabalenka, who two years ago played what was then the fourth-latest women's match in tournament history, has also experienced the knock-on effects of finishing after midnight.She is not a fan of such late starts and the disruption they can cause to an athlete's routine."When you finish late, the next day shifts a lot," Sabalenka said. "Like, you still need to get your hours of sleep, so you start later. You just can really mess up your schedule."That is at the heart of the debate surrounding the US Open's night sessions. The spectacle of late-night tennis can be a major attraction for fans, broadcasters and the tournament itself. But for the athletes, a match finishing at 2 am can have consequences that extend well beyond the final point.With four of the latest 17 finishes in tournament history already coming this year, the question is no longer simply whether New York's tennis nights can continue deep into the morning.It is whether they should.For Navratilova, the answer appears increasingly clear: "This is not sustainable…".
Article Summary: Three of the first six night sessions at the US Open finished after 2 am (local time) and two others extended beyond 1 am. The unusually late endings have prompted several players to question whether the scheduling has gone too far. A late finish does not simply mean a player leaves the court later. It can affect meals, recovery, sleep and preparation for the following day.

Article Title: Inside Taylor Townsend’s emotional journey from adversity to another US Open run, shaped by motherhood and resilience
Article Text:
Inside Taylor Townsend’s emotional journey from adversity to another US Open run, shaped by motherhood and resilience

Taylor Townsend built a different path after becoming a mother

Taylor Townsend continues to write her own tennis story

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Taylor Townsend’s 2026 US Open run ended with a 6-4, 6-3 loss to World No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka, but the American still leaves New York with another strong singles showing. The 30-year-old reached the fourth round for the second straight year after beating Diana Shnaider in three sets. Before facing Sabalenka, Townsend had also produced one of the best serving performances of her career, winning all 23 first-serve points against Taylah Preston. Her latest run is another part of a career shaped by setbacks, motherhood and a major rise in doubles.Townsend’s career has never followed a simple route. She made headlines as a teenager, but her progress was affected by difficult experiences away from the court. She has also spoken about problems involving her early earnings and how those experiences changed the way she handled her career.Motherhood later became another major part of her story. Townsend gave birth to her son, Adyn Aubrey, in March 2021 and returned to competition the following year. Since then, she has continued to compete at the highest level while balancing professional tennis with raising her son.Rather than seeing motherhood as the end of her career, Townsend has treated it as part of her motivation.She has also spoken about wanting her son to have a different experience from some of the things she went through as a child.Her doubles career has been especially successful. Townsend became the WTA’s No. 1 doubles player in July 2025 and has won five doubles titles, including Grand Slam success. She is currently No. 2 in the doubles rankings and is coached by Roger Tyzzer.That success has helped Townsend build confidence in singles too. At this year’s US Open, her serve became one of the biggest strengths of her game. Against Preston, she won every point behind her first serve and hit eight aces. Afterward, she joked about whether she had become a “servebot.”“I don’t know. I think they call this a ‘servebot.’ Am I a servebot now? Maybe.”She then credited Reilly Opelka with helping popularize the term among tennis fans.Townsend’s fourth-round appearance also added to a growing list of memorable US Open moments. She famously defeated then-World No. 4 Simona Halep at the 2019 tournament and reached the fourth round again this year after beating Shnaider 6-2, 6-7(3), 6-3.Against Sabalenka, Townsend had to deal with a completely different challenge. The defending champion and world No. 1 used her power and consistency to win in straight sets and move into the quarterfinals.Still, Townsend’s tournament showed how far her singles game has come. Her aggressive return position, left-handed serve and willingness to move forward make her uncomfortable for opponents, while her doubles experience has given her another advantage at the net.The result against Sabalenka ended this year’s singles campaign in New York, but it did not erase what Townsend had already achieved. She reached the fourth round at a Grand Slam again while continuing to compete as one of the world’s best doubles players.For Townsend, that is another step in a career she has built on her own terms. Her story now includes elite doubles success, motherhood and a renewed singles run - all after years in which many people were unsure where her career would go.
Article Summary: Taylor Townsend reached the fourth round of the US Open for the second straight year. The 30-year-old lost 6-4, 6-3 to World No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka. Townsend's career has been shaped by setbacks, motherhood and a major rise in doubles.

Article Title: How Tom Brady's post-divorce life became a masterclass in putting kids first when cameras never look away
Article Text:
Tom Brady post divorce life (Getty Images)

Is Tom Brady actually putting his kids first, or is that just his public image?

Tom Brady’s love life (Getty Images)

What does Tom Brady's dating life actually look like right now?

How is Brady redefining what it means to be a present father after divorce?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Tom Brady has done a lot of complicated things in his career. Seven Super Bowls. Three teams. One unretirement. But nothing he has faced on a football field comes close to what he is navigating now — raising three kids across two co-parenting arrangements while the entire celebrity press corps watches his every dinner reservation. Brady shares his oldest son Jack, born in 2007, with ex-girlfriend Bridget Moynahan, and has two more children -- Benjamin and Vivian with ex-wife Gisele Bündchen, from whom he divorced in 2022. The bachelor label followed almost instantly. The father label, he has never let go.At the Fortune Global Forum in New York in late 2024, Brady addressed the room plainly: "All of the parents in the room know that being a parent is probably the hardest job all of us have and we screw up a lot -- and I've screwed up a lot as a parent." That is not the line of someone carefully managing optics. It is the kind of admission that lands differently when you say it with millions of people watching.The Netflix roast in 2024 gave that tension a very specific shape. Brady called it a "parenting mistake" after his kids came to him the next morning and asked, "What was the point of that? Why did you do that?" He had gone into the roast expecting to laugh at himself publicly.He came out of it with a conversation that, in his words, felt like "a stake through the heart.""They're protective of their mom, of their dad -- of everybody," he said. "You do things as a parent that you think are one way, and then you realize after that it affected the people you care about the most."That is the balance Brady is actually managing. Not the celebrity-bachelor angle the tabloids prefer. The real work is quieter — and a lot messier.Brady sparked dating rumors with TikTok star Alix Earle during a New Year's Eve getaway to St. Barths at the end of 2025, where videos circulated of the pair getting close at a party. Before that, insiders confirmed in early 2025 that Brady and supermodel Irina Shayk had rekindled their on-again, off-again romance, with a source telling Page Six: "Tom and Irina have started dating each other again and are open to see where things go. "What is notable is how carefully Brady keeps any of this away from his children's orbit. A source told Page Six after his retirement that Brady was "all about the kids" and that while friends wanted to set him up, his focus was squarely on family life. Whether that has shifted since is hard to say definitively -- but the pattern of keeping his romantic life at arm's length from his parental one is consistent.As of 2026, Brady has not confirmed any exclusive relationship. In interviews, he has emphasized that his priorities are his children and his post-football career.Tom Brady's most revealing moment this past year was not a paparazzi photo. It was a newsletter. In his 199 newsletter, written partly as a response to golfer Scottie Scheffler's comments about prioritizing fatherhood over athletic greatness, Brady wrote: "My dedication to the sport, the hours of practice, the moments when I was laser focused -- those were times when I believe I was doing the best possible thing for my family and my kids, by prioritizing my profession. "He pushed further: "Reading bedtime stories and helping them with homework are not the only ways to be a great parent. And neither is winning Super Bowls or MVPs."It reads, on one level, as a direct response to Gisele's 2022 comment to *Elle*: "I have my children, and I would like him to be more present. I've definitely had those conversations with him over and over again." On another level, it is Brady articulating something he has been working through in real time -- that being a good father does not look the same for every man, and the public version of his life rarely tells the whole story.He also publicly praised his co-parenting relationship with Bridget Moynahan, writing: "To raise a son in the healthiest environment -- and I know we've all done that -- and it shows."With Gisele, he has maintained a similar philosophy. "I think that myself and their mom have done an amazing job of providing that solid base and foundation," he told Entertainment Tonight. "We're never a finished product. The kids aren't finished products. We're learning along with them."
Article Summary: Tom Brady has three children with two different women. Brady has not confirmed any exclusive relationship. He has maintained a similar philosophy to ex-wife Gisele Bündchen. Brady said in 2024: "I've screwed up a lot as a parent"

Article Title: Inspiring story of the day: “My grandfather always told me to focus on the Three Cs: Cabeza, Corazón y Cojones” - How Carlos Alcaraz turned three generations of family love into tennis immortality
Article Text:
Inspiring story of the day: “My grandfather always told me to focus on the Three Cs: Cabeza, Corazón y Cojones” - How Carlos Alcaraz turned three generations of family love into tennis immortality

What did Carlos Alcaraz’s grandfather teach him about the Three Cs

Why did Carlos Alcaraz get the Three Cs tattoo

How did Juan Carlos Ferrero become like a second father to Carlos Alcaraz

How have Carlos Alcaraz’s family lessons followed him into tennis history

Carlos Alcaraz’s rise to seven Grand Slam titles has been shaped by more than his talent on the tennis court. A lesson from his grandfather, Carlos Alcaraz Lerma, became one of the most personal parts of his career: “Cabeza, corazón y cojones” - head, heart and courage. Alcaraz later had the three Cs tattooed on his wrist as a reminder of that message. His close relationship with former world No. 1 Juan Carlos Ferrero also played a major role in his development. Together, those family and coaching ties helped shape the player who became the youngest man to complete the Career Grand Slam in 2026.The phrase came from Alcaraz’s grandfather and stayed with him as he grew up in El Palmar, Murcia. The three words are “Cabeza, corazón y cojones”, which mean head, heart and courage, with the final Spanish word being a much stronger and more informal expression.For Alcaraz, the idea was simple. He needed his head to make the right decisions, his heart to play with passion and courage to take risks when the pressure was highest.Alcaraz has spoken about the message before, saying:“My grandfather always told me to focus on the Three Cs: head, heart, and balls.”The words became closely linked with his identity as a player. His tennis is built around attacking shots, quick movement and a willingness to try difficult plays even when a match is going against him.The story also has a strong family connection. Alcaraz’s grandfather was involved with tennis in El Palmar, where the young player spent part of his early years around the sport.That makes the “Three Cs” more than a slogan. It is a piece of advice that Alcaraz has carried from his childhood into the biggest matches of his career.After breaking through at the highest level, Alcaraz chose to keep his grandfather’s message with him permanently. In 2022, he got a CCC tattoo, representing “Cabeza, Corazón y Cojones.”The tattoo became a visible reminder of the words that had followed him through his early tennis career. Reports at the time said the tattoo was placed on his wrist and was connected directly to his grandfather’s motto.The timing was also significant. Alcaraz had just enjoyed the breakthrough season that changed his career. He won his first Masters 1000 title in Miami in April 2022 and then won his first Grand Slam at the US Open later that year.By September 2022, he had also become the youngest player to reach No. 1 in the ATP rankings at 19 years and four months. He finished that season as the youngest year-end No. 1 in ATP history.The tattoo therefore came during the period when Alcaraz was moving from a highly rated teenager to one of the biggest names in tennis.Rather than choosing a trophy or a tournament date, he picked something tied to his family.Alcaraz’s grandfather gave him the message, but Juan Carlos Ferrero became one of the most important people in turning that young talent into a top-level player.Ferrero, a former world No. 1 and 2003 French Open champion, began working with Alcaraz when the Spaniard was a teenager. Alcaraz trained at Ferrero’s academy in Villena, Spain, and their relationship grew far beyond normal coach-player duties.Alcaraz has openly described Ferrero as his mentor and second father.“He was my mentor. Everything that I’ve done is thanks to him. I learned a lot, not only professionally, but the personal part as well. He’s my second father… I am the person and the player I am today thanks to him.”Those comments came after years of working together. Ferrero also described Alcaraz as being like a fourth child to him, showing how close the relationship had become.One of the most emotional moments in their relationship came in 2022. Ferrero’s father, Eduardo Ferrero, died suddenly in March while Juan Carlos was in the United States with Alcaraz. Ferrero returned to Spain for the funeral before coming back to Miami, where Alcaraz was preparing for the tournament final.Alcaraz went on to beat Casper Ruud 7-5, 6-4 in the Miami final to win his first Masters 1000 title. Afterward, the two shared an emotional moment.Their professional partnership eventually ended in December 2025 after about seven years. Even then, Alcaraz made clear how much Ferrero had meant to his career, calling their time together an important chapter of his life.The clearest proof of Alcaraz’s growth came in 2026.He entered the Australian Open without a title at Melbourne Park, but defeated Novak Djokovic in the final to win his seventh Grand Slam. That victory completed all four major titles for Alcaraz: the US Open, Wimbledon, Roland Garros and Australian Open.At 22 years and 272 days, he became the youngest man to complete the Career Grand Slam in the Open Era.His Grand Slam record now includes two US Open titles, two Wimbledon titles, two French Open titles and one Australian Open title.Even with those achievements, the idea behind the Three Cs remains easy to understand. Head is about making good decisions. Heart is about loving the game. Courage is about taking the shot when the moment demands it.That message began with his grandfather and became part of Alcaraz’s identity long before he was winning major trophies. His tattoo keeps those words close, while the years with Ferrero helped him learn how to handle the pressure that comes with becoming a champion.And now, at 23, Alcaraz is already a seven-time major winner and a Career Grand Slam champion. His records have grown, but the family lesson behind the three letters has stayed remarkably simple.
Article Summary: Carlos Alcaraz is the youngest man to complete the Career Grand Slam in 2026. The Spaniard has won seven Grand Slam titles in his career. His grandfather taught him to focus on the Three Cs: head, heart and balls. Juan Carlos Ferrero was one of the most important people in his development. Ferrero's father, Eduardo, died suddenly in March 2022.

Article Title: “I never thought I was going to do it”: Cole Johnson reveals how a joke suddenly turned into a real fight after a huge offer came his way
Article Text:

Cole Johnson says a joke changed when people started offering him serious money

Fans are questioning whether Cole Johnson’s dangerous challenge should happen at all

Cole Johnson did not expect a joke about fighting a chimpanzee to become a real fight proposal. The 1-0 amateur MMA fighter, better known as Wavy MMA, says an offhand claim turned into serious money offers and a proposed pay-per-view event. Now, a reported September 11 date has put his bizarre challenge in the spotlight. The bigger question is no longer whether Johnson believes he can win. It is whether this fight should happen at all.Johnson did not begin with plans to actually fight a chimpanzee.The idea started with a video he made as a joke. But the reaction online quickly changed things when people began reaching out to him with serious offers.Johnson said one person offered him $500,000 to take part in a fight involving a chimpanzee in an unnamed country. He eventually agreed to explore the opportunity, but the arrangement fell apart after he decided the person behind it could not be trusted.That could have been the end of it.Instead, Johnson claims another offer came along for even more money. He has not revealed the amount, but says the people behind the new proposal appeared more trustworthy.A promotional website for the event has since appeared online, with a reported September 11 date.The location has not been publicly revealed.The attention surrounding the proposed matchup has also pushed Johnson to explain how he believes such a confrontation could work.He says the chimpanzee would not have its teeth or claws removed. He has also claimed that people with tranquilizers would be nearby in case the situation became too dangerous.Johnson has made it clear that he knows there is a serious risk involved.“I don’t want to kill this wild animal and I don’t want to die,” he said while discussing the proposed fight.That admission is important because Johnson is not describing the matchup as a normal MMA contest.A human opponent understands the rules, knows when a referee can stop the fight and can choose to tap out. A chimpanzee would not understand any of those things.Johnson still believes his years of training could give him a chance.His background is built around wrestling and grappling, and he appears confident that those skills could help him control the animal if the situation allows it.But that confidence comes with a clear warning.Johnson has admitted that he could suffer a serious injury during the encounter. He has even discussed the need to protect vulnerable parts of his body because he knows the animal would not fight like a trained MMA opponent.The money may have helped turn the idea into something more serious, but Johnson's comments suggest he understands that the potential consequences could be far more important than the payday.Once news of the proposed fight spread, the reaction from fans was largely filled with concern and disbelief.Some people online questioned whether the event was even genuine. Others immediately focused on the safety issues surrounding it.The question of animal welfare has also become impossible to ignore.In a normal MMA fight, both competitors agree to participate. They train for combat, understand what is expected of them and know there are rules designed to protect them.That is why this proposed event raises questions that go far beyond whether Johnson could win.Even if organizers have medical personnel and tranquilizers nearby, stopping an animal in the middle of an aggressive encounter is not the same as stopping a human fighter.There is also no guarantee that a situation would remain under control long enough for anyone to intervene.Johnson himself has acknowledged that a serious injury is possible.“I’m not saying I’m going to come out of this thing unscathed,” he said.That statement has given fans another reason to question the entire idea.Some online reactions have been blunt, with viewers predicting severe injuries and questioning how the event could possibly be legal or ethical.Others have simply dismissed the proposed fight as something that will never happen.For now, there are still plenty of unanswered questions.The location has not been revealed, the exact rules remain unclear and there is uncertainty over what kind of oversight would actually be in place.The existence of a promotional website and a countdown does not necessarily mean the event is ready to happen as advertised.What is clear is that Johnson's original joke has grown far beyond what he expected. He reportedly never planned to take the idea seriously. Then the offers started arriving.Now, the 1-0 fighter finds himself at the center of a bizarre combat-sports story that has sparked debates about money, personal risk, animal welfare and the limits of fight entertainment.But Johnson's own words explain why the story has caught so much attention. What began as a joke became a serious proposition once someone was willing to pay him to prove whether his confidence was justified.
Article Summary: Cole Johnson says an offhand claim turned into serious money offers and a proposed pay-per-view event. A promotional website for the event has since appeared online, with a reported September 11 date. Johnson has admitted that he could suffer a serious injury during the encounter. He has also discussed the need to protect vulnerable parts of his body because the animal would not fight like a trained MMA opponent.

But a late charge from teammate Kimi Antonelli changed everything, leaving Russell with second place after a race that came down to strategy, tire life and a tense fight between the two Mercedes cars.Russell had a strong start to the race and soon moved ahead of pole sitter Pierre Gasly. From there, he looked comfortable at the front while Antonelli faced a much bigger challenge.The Italian had started from 19th on the grid. Despite that difficult position, Antonelli made rapid progress through the field and soon found himself fighting near the front.The situation became even more interesting when a Virtual Safety Car was introduced after Lance Stroll's Aston Martin stopped on track.Mercedes then split its strategy.Antonelli was brought into the pits for fresh tires, while Russell remained on the circuit. The decision initially sent Antonelli backward, but the fresher tires gave him an important advantage for the closing stages.Russell said he had expected a different approach from Mercedes.“To be honest I thought we were both going to stay out. I was surprised to see him pit,” he said.As the race moved toward its final laps, Russell began to struggle with his tires. He had stayed out on the same hard tire, leaving him with less grip as Antonelli closed the gap.“I was just struggling with the tyres towards the end,” Russell explained.Antonelli eventually got close enough to make his move. With only a few laps left, he passed Russell and took control of the race.The Italian then held on to win at his home circuit, while Russell finished second.For Russell, it was a frustrating way to lose a race he had led for so long. Still, he recognized how quickly the balance had shifted.Russell could have easily focused on the disappointment of losing the victory. Instead, he gave credit to Mercedes for taking a calculated risk.The split strategy meant one driver would benefit if the fresh tires proved decisive, while the other had track position. There was no guarantee which approach would work better.“I think at the end it was a roll of the dice both ways,” Russell said.He also explained that the team could not have known for certain which choice would produce the better result.“In the moment, the team wouldn't have known which strategy was better. It made sense to split the cars but, in the end, Kimi had great pace, and there we are.”That final point was important. Antonelli did not simply benefit from the strategy. He still had to use the opportunity, and his pace allowed him to catch and pass Russell before the checkered flag.Russell was quick to praise his teammate.“Huge congratulations to Kimi of course, an incredible result from him,” he said.The victory was especially significant for Antonelli because it came at his home race after starting from the back of the field.Russell, meanwhile, was left with the feeling that second place was still a step in the right direction after a difficult period.“I'll take it, it's been more positive than it was pre-summer break and that's what I needed to try and achieve,” he said.There was still no hiding what he wanted most.“Of course I would have loved to be P1 today.”The result extended Antonelli's Drivers' Championship lead to 66 points, while Russell strengthened his position in second ahead of Lewis Hamilton.Monza therefore delivered two very different outcomes for Mercedes. Antonelli celebrated a dream home victory, while Russell had to accept that his teammate and a different tire strategy had turned a likely win into another podium.
Article Summary: Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli wins Italian Grand Prix at Monza. George Russell finishes second after struggling with his tires. Russell accepts Mercedes' strategy gamble despite missing out on P1. Antoneelli extends his Drivers' Championship lead to 66 points.

Article Title: 'I am so sorry': Moroccan World Cup star rushed to hospital with injury so horrific it leaves rival keeper in tears

The severity of the injury quickly became apparent, leaving Siampanis visibly shaken.The goalkeeper broke down in tears while medical staff attended to the Olympiacos forward, clearly distressed by the accidental collision.Players from both teams were equally stunned. Olympiacos and Volos stars immediately waved frantically for medical assistance and called for the medical team to hurry onto the pitch.After several minutes of treatment, El Kaabi was carried from the pitch on a stretcher to applause from those inside the stadium.Armando Gonzalez came on in his place.The referee awarded Olympiacos a penalty following the incident, with Jota Silva stepping up to convert from the spot.The midfielder dedicated his celebration to El Kaabi, an emotional gesture that reflected the shock among his teammates after seeing the severity of the injury.El Kaabi was then taken to hospital, where he underwent tests to determine the full extent of the damage.Reports in Greece have claimed that he is expected to undergo surgery, while initial medical estimates suggest the striker could be sidelined for six to seven months.That timeline would represent a major blow for both Olympiacos and the Moroccan national team.Siampanis later addressed the incident himself, using his personal Instagram account to apologise directly to El Kaabi.“I am deeply sorry for what happened today, Ayoub,” the goalkeeper wrote, reiterating his deep regret over the devastating collision.Olympiacos also sent a message of support to their striker through the club's official channels.“Ayoub, in this difficult moment, the entire Olympiacos family stands by your side with all our hearts,” the club wrote.“Your strength, passion and fighting spirit have inspired us so many times. Now it’s our turn to send all that strength back to you.”The injury came during a frustrating night for Olympiacos, who were held to a 1-1 draw by Volos and now sit second in the Greek league behind rivals AEK Athens.El Kaabi has been an important part of the side since joining the Greek giants in 2023, scoring an impressive 82 goals in 139 appearances.His form has also made him a regular presence for Morocco.He was included in Morocco's squad for the World Cup in North America this summer, making one appearance at the tournament.El Kaabi came on as a 70th-minute substitute during Morocco's 4-2 victory over Haiti in Group C.For now, however, football has taken a back seat.The striker faces a lengthy period on the sidelines after an injury that left his teammates and opponents visibly shaken.Siampanis could barely contain his emotions on the pitch and later felt compelled to apologise publicly to the player involved.Olympiacos have made their feelings clear too: they will be behind El Kaabi throughout what could be a six-to-seven-month road back.

Article Title: 'They're clearly hoping to kill him in there': Imran Khan's sons raise serious concerns
Article Text:
