The sons of former Pakistan captain and Prime Minister Imran Khan have strongly criticised Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) chairman Mohsin Naqvi after the board was accused of threatening to abandon the Lord’s Test against England. Sulaiman and Kasim Khan also raised serious concerns about their father's health and conditions in prison, claiming that Pakistan authorities are trying to silence him.The controversy began during the second Test at Lord’s after Sky Sports aired an interview conducted by former England captain Michael Atherton with Sulaiman and Kasim.They spoke about their father's health and his conditions in prison.Reports later claimed that the PCB threatened not to send the Pakistan team out for the post-lunch session on the first day unless the interview was taken off air.With Mohsin Naqvi facing increased scrutiny, the sons also spoke about their concerns over Khan's solitary confinement.Kasim made a serious allegation about the former Pakistan captain's safety.“They're clearly hoping to kill him in there. They want to silence him as secretly as possible and just slowly make him fade into nothing.“That's a very difficult thing to do with the most popular person in Pakistan right now.Their strategy, whenever we speak, is to let everything fizzle out and then impose more brutal restrictions that make it even harder for him to survive.”Kasim criticised the PCB's reported reaction and said the board had damaged its own image.“They made absolute fools of themselves,” Kasim told The Telegraph on Sunday.Sulaiman said he was surprised that the PCB reacted so strongly to an interview about his father.“I was expecting some sort of response. But I didn't think they would be so tactless as to threaten not to take to the field.“It shouldn't be in the remit of the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) to ask for an interview about an ex-Pakistan player, somebody who lived in England for 22 years, to be taken down. This wasn't about politics, but about the humanitarian situation and his health.”Pakistani authorities have repeatedly denied allegations of mistreatment and have maintained that Khan is receiving proper medical care.Sulaiman, however, questioned those assurances and said the family had not been given enough information about his father's condition.“The worrying theory we're hearing is that they're drip-feeding these reports of his ailing health and pretending that they're trying to help him, just to lay the ground for something worse to happen. Then they can wash their hands and say: 'He's just an old man who died, and we had nothing to do with it.’“They haven't given us proof of any of this. It's all just hearsay from government sources – there's no transparency, they don't want to give anyone access, so how are we supposed to believe any of it? The last verifiable piece of information we had was from him, six months ago, when he spoke about his eye and how it had been neglected.”
Article Summary: Sulaiman and Kasim Khan have criticised Pakistan Cricket Board chairman Mohsin Naqvi. The board was accused of threatening to abandon the Lord’s Test against England. The sons also raised serious concerns about their father's health and conditions in prison.

Article Title: 'Win against India damaged us a lot': Mohammad Yousuf explains Pakistan cricket's decline
Article Text:
ICC Photo

'That match... damaged us a lot'

Players wanted to become captain

Pakistan in trouble in England

'It's not just this one series'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think the PCB was right to make changes in the team during the England tour? Yes, it was necessary. No, better to wait for the series to end. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Former Pakistan star cricketer Mohammad Yousuf has said the country's current cricket crisis began after their famous 10-wicket win over India at the 2021 T20 World Cup in Dubai.Pakistan had never beaten India in a World Cup before that match. Babar Azam scored an unbeaten 68, while Mohammad Rizwan made 79 not out as Pakistan chased down 152 without losing a wicket. The win was celebrated as a historic moment for Pakistan cricket.However, Yousuf believes the victory also changed the mindset of the players and played a role in the team's decline in the years that followed.Yousuf said the players became too confident after beating India and failed to understand what they needed to do next.“That match which we won against India in 2021, that damaged us a lot. Because after that victory, players started to think that they had achieved something big. They couldn’t understand what they had to do next. When you are performing well, you should stay humble. If you behave with your collar raised, and get disrespectful, problems will arrive. And a lot of them have arrived in Pakistan cricket,” said Yousuf in a conversation on Samaa TV.Yousuf believes the problem was not only about Pakistan's results. He feels the team's attitude also changed after the famous win.Yousuf also blamed the fight for captaincy for some of Pakistan's problems.He said players became more interested in becoming the team's captain instead of taking responsibility for their performances.“Everyone in the team was trying to become the captain of the Pakistan team. The consequences are still hurting Pakistan cricket. Look at all the cricket Pakistan has played in the last four-five years, from ODI World Cups, T20 World Cups to Asia Cups and Champions Trophy. There has been terrible cricket. The PCB has been supporting you throughout. So many coaches have come and gone, so many things have changed just to try and help the Pakistan team. But no player has stood up and taken responsibility. Eventually, PCB had to take a step that it did. I back what PCB did,” added Yousuf.Yousuf's comments have come at a difficult time for Pakistan cricket. The team suffered heavy defeats in the first two Tests against England. Pakistan lost the Headingley Test by an innings and 103 runs before suffering a 194-run defeat at Lord's. The Pakistan Cricket Board then made major changes in the middle of the England tour.Seven players - Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq, Salman Ali Agha, Ali Usman, Khurram Shahzad, Aamir Jamal and Muhammad Awais Jafar - were sent back to Pakistan with one Test still left in the series.The PCB also removed head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed and assistant coach Umar Gul. Seven replacements were called up, including five uncapped players.The decision to make major changes in the middle of a Test series attracted a lot of attention. However, Yousuf said he had no problem with the PCB's decision.When asked whether the board was right to take action with one Test still remaining, he said: “Yes, there is no issue with when PCB have taken action. The Pakistan team is ninth in the World Test Championship standings. They are ninth because there are only nine teams in the table. Pakistan ka naam kharab ho raha hai (Pakistan’s reputation is getting ruined). So when that’s happening, the board has to take some steps to improve. ”Yousuf also suggested that something may have happened inside the dressing room that led to the seven players being sent home.Yousuf said Pakistan's problems cannot be blamed only on the ongoing England series.He pointed to the team's poor performances in major tournaments over the last few years.“I don’t see an issue with the PCB reaction. Because the team has been playing terrible cricket. It’s not just this one series against England. We played in the T20 World Cup final in 2022 and played in an Asia Cup final as well, but since those finals, just look at the performances coming out of this Pakistan team,” Yousuf said.Pakistan have struggled across formats in recent years. They were swept 2-0 by Bangladesh earlier this year, their second 0-2 series defeat against the same opposition after the 2024 home series.The team's poor performances have raised questions over its leadership, selection and overall direction.But for Yousuf, the root of the problem goes back to that famous night in Dubai in 2021, when Pakistan finally beat India by 10 wickets in a World Cup match.
Article Summary: Former Pakistan star Mohammad Yousuf says the country's current cricket crisis began after their famous 10-wicket win over India at the 2021 T20 World Cup in Dubai. He believes the victory also changed the mindset of the players and played a role in the team's decline in the years that followed. He also blamed the fight for captaincy for some of Pakistan's problems.

Article Title: How Ciara's pregnancy reveal skipped the glam photoshoot and still became the most-talked-about post of the year
Article Text:
Ciara is pregnant at 40 with her fifth child (Instagram)

Why did Ciara's pregnancy announcement go viral without a traditional photoshoot?

Did Russell Wilson always want a fifth child with Ciara?

How does baby No. 5 fit into Ciara and Russell Wilson's family?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

On Sunday, September 6, Ciara posted a pregnancy announcement on Instagram that had nothing to do with a staged studio setup or a carefully lit maternity shoot. No wardrobe team, no dramatic backdrop. Just a backyard, a clothesline, four named shirts, and a blank onesie hanging at the end. Seven words in the caption -- "One more person to Love" and the internet did the rest. For a couple that has spent years building one of the most publicly documented families in entertainment, this one landed differently.Most celebrity baby reveals follow a formula. Professional photographer, curated setting, coordinated outfits. Ciara threw all of that out on Sunday. She appeared in a white tank top, low-rise jeans, and hair curlers -- looking every bit like someone who had not planned to impress anyone. The video panned slowly across four white shirts hanging in the sun, each one bearing a child's name: Future, Sienna, Win, Amora. Then came the tiny onesie at the end, blank, unnamed, carrying the entire weight of the announcement without saying a single word.She turned toward the camera with a wide smile, held up five fingers, and that was it. No narration needed. The visual did the work that most announcements spend thousands of dollars trying to manufacture. That authenticity is exactly why it cut through.Vanessa Bryant was among the first to respond, writing in the comments, "It's about damn time. I love you guys so much!!!!! Sooooo happy for you." La La Anthony followed with, "Another beautiful blessing!!! More to love!!!" When your comment section fills up like that within minutes, the post has already won.The answer to that is not even close to a maybe. At Fanatics Fest in New York City on July 17, Wilson told E! News, "We have four amazing kids and I'm trying to convince Ciara to have a fifth. Cinco, you got to be on the way soon." He was smiling when he said it, but the intent was clear. He added, "I want to have five, Ciara does too. We'll see. Hopefully, I can convince her."Ciara revealed to Us Weekly in July that Wilson had actually brought up the idea of a fifth child shortly after she gave birth to Amora, prompting her to tell him to slow down. That detail matters. This was not a spontaneous decision made in the summer of 2026. Russell had been quietly lobbying for "Cinco" for nearly two years before Sunday's post made the nickname official. When Wilson dropped "Baby Cinco!" in the comments, it was the kind of callback that only lands when you have been saying the same thing for a long time and you finally get to be right.The baby will be Ciara's fifth child overall and her fourth with Wilson. The couple's blended family includes Future Zahir Wilburn, 12, Ciara's son from her previous relationship with rapper Future; Sienna Princess, 9; Win Harrison, 6; and Amora Princess, 2. Wilson has been stepfather to Future Zahir since the boy was a toddler, and he has never treated that role as secondary.Ciara told USA Today in 2025, "Being a mom is my favorite job of all because it really is a job. And God is amazing. I have my four precious babies, Amora, Sienna, Win, and Future, but my husband is my biggest baby."The timing here is worth noting. Wilson retired from the NFL in June 2026 after 14 seasons and joined CBS Sports as an analyst on The NFL Today. A new career chapter, a 10th wedding anniversary in July, and now a fifth baby on the way. The announcement did not feel like a one-off post. It felt like a household that had made several big decisions at once and was ready to share all of them.No due date or gender has been confirmed. The onesie at the end of that clothesline remains blank, and for now, that is exactly the point.
Article Summary: Ciara posted a pregnancy announcement on Instagram on Sunday. The video had nothing to do with a staged studio setup or a carefully lit maternity shoot. The baby will be Ciara's fifth child overall and her fourth with Russell Wilson. No due date or gender has been confirmed.

Article Title: MP's 'Bittu Tabahi' who cleaned river solo, gets praise from Kevin Pietersen, job offer from Ocean Cleanup
Article Text:
A young student received a job offer from a global environmental organization

Kevin Pietersen praised Bittu's effort as 'heroic'

Poll Vote & Share your view Should individuals fund their own environmental initiatives like Bittu did? Yes, it promotes personal responsibility Only if they can afford it No, funding should come from organizations 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





BHOPAL: In a striking turn of events, Surendra Singh Choudhary, the 21-year-old Madhya Pradesh student known online as 'Bittu Tabahi', on Sunday received a job offer from The Ocean Cleanup, a Netherlands-based environmental NGO, after former England cricketer Kevin Pietersen hailed his solo river-cleaning drive as "heroic".The offer, extended by Boyan Slat, founder and CEO of the organisation, marks a rapid escalation from local initiative to global recognition for the Biaora youth."I received a call from Slat this morning," Bittu told TOI. "He was exceedingly pleased with my work, and he took down my credentials. I'm rather excited about it." When asked which job had been offered, he said, "That wasn't discussed. I'm told they'll get back to me soon."Bittu began his cleanup of the plastic-choked Ajnar river in Biaora, Rajgarh district, on Jan 26, spending his own money- around Rs 30,000-to buy basic tools and supplies. He cleaned up three major ghats.Without gloves, proper footwear, or even the ability to swim, he waded into the polluted waters to remove trash, algae and debris, documenting the transformation in before-and-after images that later went viral.His persistence drew attention from industrialist Anand Mahindra, MP CM Mohan Yadav and thousands of social media users. The momentum grew when cricket legend Kevin Pietersen shared Bittu's story on Instagram, calling his effort "heroic" and saying it deserved international recognition.Pietersen highlighted how the young man entered the river barefoot and without protective gear, taking action instead of waiting for authorities. Soon after, Boyan Slat, founder of The Ocean Cleanup, responded to a post about Bittu's work with a simple invitation: "Come work for us.""My aim was never personal credit but to inspire others," Bittu said.
Article Summary: Kevin Pietersen praised Bittu's effort as 'heroic' The Ocean Cleanup, a Netherlands-based environmental NGO, has offered the student a job. The offer marks a rapid escalation from local initiative to global recognition for the Biaora youth.

Article Title: Chaos at Hyderabad’s Jubilee Hills pub: Rival groups clash, 2 injured; 3 cases filed
Article Text:
Two individuals sustained injuries during a drunken brawl at a Jubilee Hills pub (Picture credits: X)

TOI

TOI





HYDERABAD: Two persons suffered injuries after rival groups clashed during a drunken brawl at a pub in Jubilee Hills late on Saturday night, triggering tension in the area. Police are tight-lipped about the incident as one of the groups was led by Congress Rajya Sabha MP Anil Kumar Yadav’s brother, Arvind Kumar Yadav. Police have booked three separate cases, two against the warring groups and another against Cara Cara pub management for operating beyond permitted hours.On Saturday night, Arvind Kumar Yadav, who is the son of former MP Anjan Kumar Yadav, went with family and friends to the pub at the hotel in Jubilee Hills. Another group, led by Wasim Khan and Afsar Khan, was also partying at the place.‘Property vandalised’“Late in the night, when Wasim and Afsar were walking close to the table where Arvind Kumar Yadav and his family were sitting, an argument broke out, which escalated into a fight between the two groups. There was palpable tension on the premises, and it was recorded in CCTV footage too. Later, both the groups left the premises and again clashed at the parking lot, where some more persons joined them,” sources in Hyderabad police toldWhen the two groups clashed inside the pub, bouncers intervened since the establishment’s property was vandalised. A large number of persons were seen going berserk again in the parking lot, damaging parked cars besides beating people. A video has gone viral where a group of persons pushed down a person and was repeatedly beaten by them. Incidentally, the drama took place after 1 am on Sunday, which was beyond the permissible time to operate the business.Through sources in Hyderabad police,came to know that the Jubilee Hills police finally registered three different cases.A suo motu case was registered against both groups for the offence of affray and the related acts of fighting. On the complaint of Wasim Khan, a case was registered for assaulting the complainant and his friend in the parking area, when they were proceeding to their residence. The accused persons reportedly intercepted their vehicle and assaulted them and damaged the car.“A case was also registered against the pub management for allegedly operating the pub beyond the permitted hours without obtaining the required permission for the extended operating hours,” police said in a late night statement on Sunday.

Police have booked three separate cases, two against the warring groups and another against Cara Cara pub management for operating beyond permitted hours. A video has gone viral where a group of persons pushed down a person and was repeatedly beaten.

Article Title: Tirumala temple deputy executive officer M Lokanadham arrested in disproportionate assets case
Article Text:
Tirumala temple's deputy executive officer M Lokanadham has been arrested by ACB officials for holding disproportionate assets





TIRUPATI: Tirumala temple deputy executive officer M Lokanadham was arrested by Anti-Corruption Bureau sleuths in connection with a disproportionate assets case registered against him on Thursday.It may be recalled that ACB teams conducted raids at Lokanadham’s residence and multiple locations linked to him and unearthed movable and immovable properties, including 2 kg of gold, 6.5 kg of silver and Rs 12.5 lakh cash, all worth approximately Rs 5 crore and disproportionate to his known sources of income, on Wednesday.ACB sleuths continued their searches for the second consecutive day on Thursday before formally taking the Tirumala temple deputy EO into custody to produce him before the ACB court at Nellore and subsequently send him to judicial remand.The timing of Lokanadham’s arrest has come as a big jolt to the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams as the Tirupati trust finds itself less than two weeks away from the Srivari annual Brahmotsavams, slated to get underway at Tirumala from Sept 15.The Tirupati trust reportedly went into a huddle to quickly find a suitable replacement within the organisation to be appointed as the Tirumala temple deputy EO, as this is a crucial post linked to the smooth functioning of the day-to-day religious rituals held at the Tirumala temple as well as the annual festivals observed at Tirumala.Even as Devasthanams employees were yet to come out of the rude shock following the arrest of the Tirumala temple deputy EO, former TTD chairman Bhumana Karunakar Reddy questioned inconsistencies in the ACB narrative linked to the disproportionate assets case in which Lokanadham was arrested.Pointing out that amid the ongoing raids on Wednesday, ACB DSP Srinivasa Rao had told reporters that following a barrage of complaints received against Lokanadham, the ACB was carrying out raids in connection with the disproportionate assets case as per the court’s direction.Interestingly, in the final ACB press release issued later on Wednesday evening, the ACB took a completely different narrative, stating that the CBI, which completed its investigation into the laddu ghee adulteration case and filed a chargesheet, had shared some information about the disproportionate assets of some TTD employees with the ACB, AP.“In follow-up action, a Disproportionate Assets case was registered against K Chinna Appanna, Personal Assistant (PA) to the then TTD Chairman YV Subba Reddy. On further enquiry and collection of evidence, now a fresh disproportionate assets case was registered on Lokanadham U/s 13(2) r/w 13(1)(b) of the Prevention of Corruption (As amended in 2018) Act, 1988.”Bhumana wondered how there could be two versions from the ACB on the disproportionate assets case booked against Lokanadham.“It was way back in January that the CBI concluded the investigation in the Laddu ghee adulteration case and had also filed its final chargesheet at the Nellore court besides submitting a self-contained note with some recommendations to the state govt. Close to 7 months after that, the ACB note claims the CBI to have shared information relating to the disproportionate assets of some Devasthanams employees, which is quite bizarre to attempt to link up the laddu case investigation to the DA case booked on Lokanadham,” the ex-TTD chief observed.Bhumana demanded that the state govt disclose the information shared by the CBI with the ACB, if such information exists in the first place, especially after its futile attempt to enforce the “red book vindictive” action against certain Devasthanams employees in the TTD.
Article Summary: Tirumala temple deputy executive officer M Lokanadham was arrested by Anti- Corruption Bureau sleuths in connection with a disproportionate assets case registered against him on Thursday. ACB teams conducted raids on Wednesday and unearthed movable and immovable properties, including 2 kg of gold, 6.5 kg of silver and Rs 12.5 lakh cash, all worth approximately Rs 5 crore.

Article Title: “Three-against-one situation”: El Rubius opens up on being “targeted” in MrBeast’s viral $1M challenge
Article Text:
El Rubius reacted honestly after his elimination from MrBeast’s $1 million challenge, calling it “unfair” and claiming he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings. His response felt real and balanced, especially after MrBeast’s team later sent him a cake, softening the moment.

El Rubius reflects on a tough and “unfair” exit

El Rubius did not just walk away from MrBeast’s $1 million streamer challenge. He opened up. Soon after his elimination, the Spanish creator shared a raw reaction with fans, giving them a closer look at what the experience felt like from inside the game. It was not polished or carefully framed. It felt real, and that is exactly why it caught attention so quickly.The clip and his response have since fueled conversations across the streaming space. Some viewers believe intense competitions like this naturally lead to uneven situations. Others feel Rubius may have had a point about being singled out. Either way, his words have added a human layer to a challenge that many only saw as entertainment.Speaking through an Instagram Story, Rubius did not hide his frustration, but he also made sure to thank his supporters. He said, "Guys, I just got knocked out of the game. It was a bit of an unfair elimination, but hey, at least I managed to walk away with $50,000 for you all, which I’ve already distributed. It went to the mods, the subs, and the non-subs alike."He further added, "I’m happy, of course, though admittedly, it was incredibly tough.I wasn't really a fan of the challenge itself, either. But then again... it was basically a three-against-one situation the entire time. I mean, they were targeting me specifically the whole way through. I kept trying to go after RaKai, but, well, he actually just got eliminated in the end. So, at least justice was served for Abraham. Abraham, if you’re watching this, we were all rooting for you, and standing right there with you."His message carried mixed emotions. There was disappointment, yes, but also pride in how he handled things. Giving away his $50,000 winnings to his community stood out as a gesture that meant more than the result itself.He continued with another honest note, saying, "And in the end, karma finally caught up with that little punk. Sorry, I’m being a bit toxic right now, but let's just hope the MrBeast team doesn't see this! Guys, thank you all so much. Seriously, thank you for all the support and for just being there."He added, "Every time I asked for something in the chat or whatever it was, you guys were right there. You’re incredible. I’m a little disappointed in myself, personally, mostly for not performing better, but hey, I gave it my all, and we still walked away with $50,000, so we’ve got to look on the bright side. All right, guys, big hugs to all my brothers out there!"Interestingly, the story did not end with frustration. Later that day, Rubius revealed that MrBeast’s team had sent him a cake after his exit. It was a small gesture, but it shifted the mood. It showed that even in a high-pressure challenge, there is still room for respect.In the end, Rubius’ reaction felt honest and grounded. That is what stayed with people.
Article Summary: El Rubius was eliminated from MrBeast's $1 million streamer challenge. He called it "unfair" and said he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings.

But for a 25-year-old techie the craze for IPL tickets for RCB vs CSK turned too costly and he was duped for a massive Rs. 1.46 lakh.The techie, a resident of B Narayanapura, fell into a trap by a post posted by a fraudster who posed himself as a ticket seller on Instagram.As per a report in Deccan Herald, the techie alleged in a complaint to Mahadevapura Police that an individual claiming to be Sumit Biswal promised he could arrange IPL tickets along with food coupons.As per the techie, Biswal was introduced him as a senior supervisor for ticket counter at M Chinnaswamy Stadium"He asked me to come near the stadium gate number 10, saying someone would deliver the tickets within minutes, and even sent an email confirmation to gain my trust," the complainant told Deccan Herald."Initially, I agreed to buy two tickets for Rs 3,700 each,but he kept asking for more money under various pretexts such as refundable security deposits, additional ID cards and food coupons.Trusting him, I made multiple payments - even using my mother’s bank account after exhausting my own limits—and ended up transferring around Rs 1.46 lakh," he added.Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s incisive spell of 3-41, coming after a marauding batting show from Tim David, Rajat Patidar and Devdutt Padikkal, propelled Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) to a commanding 43-run victory over Chennai Super Kings (CSK) in their IPL 2026 encounter at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium on Sunday.The contest saw RCB’s batting unit dismantle CSK’s attack with relentless hitting, as David’s 70 not out off just 25 balls and Patidar’s unbeaten 48 off only 19 balls provided for the late fireworks after Padikkal’s fluent 50 off 29 balls had set the tone for the daunting total.Their combined effort lifted RCB to a daunting 250/3, thus setting a new record for highest total in IPL 2026. Article Title: "Trans women are.....": Clavicular’s viral moment with trans women sparks fresh conversation on internet culture
Article Text:
A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Instead of conflict, the exchange highlights shared influence and mutual awareness. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration rather than ownership.

Clavicular and trans women share a surprising realization about online trends

The video of Clavicular, a short-video producer, is going around the Internet, yet not the reason why. There is no yelling or over-the-top drama. It is a mere, everyday talk that seems almost novel nowadays, in the age of internet, which is overflowing with content. The scene is easy-going, the tone of the narrative is straightforward, and the characters appear more concerned with conversation than combat.The message that is being addressed is the flow of the conversation. It discusses internet culture, the way people communicate with one another and the place of trends. Rather than bringing out a debate, the encounter towards curiosity. It quietly brings attention to something that a lot of people who use the internet notice but don't often say out loud. People in different communities often have a bigger impact on each other than they think.The conversation begins with a confident and lighthearted comment from one of the trans women present. She says, "You know that trans women are like the OG lip masters, right? We are very talented in the program. Like, I do the peptides, I'm on Zeta." Her tone carries a mix of pride and humor, setting a relaxed vibe at the table.Clavicular responds in a way that keeps the mood steady but adds a different angle.He says, "That is funny because you guys were using a lot of the words in like the South Korean subreddits in like 2014." It’s not confrontational. If anything, it feels like an observation. He points to how certain words and ideas may have traveled across different online spaces over time.Another voice joins in and brings the moment full circle. "Guys, we're like the OGs. I saw a couple of posts about that. We're like copying each other." That line hits in a simple but honest way. It reflects something familiar. Online culture is rarely created in isolation. It grows through sharing, borrowing, and sometimes even unknowingly repeating.That's what makes the clip so powerful. It doesn't want to make a point or win an argument. It only shows a group of people talking, listening, and figuring something out together.This moment feels different in a space where viral content often leads to fights. It reminds people that conversations can be calm, thoughtful, and still important. And sometimes, that honest silence is what makes it work.
Article Summary: A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration.

Article Title: Maharashtra horror: Teen murdered, body dumped near Mini Seashore
Article Text:
A 19-year-old man was found murdered near a public garden in Vashi





NAVI MUMBAI: A 19-year-old boy was murdered and his body was dumped on the pavement near a public garden along Mini Seashore Road in Sector 10A, Vashi, early on Saturday morning. The Vashi police have registered a murder case against unidentified accused.Shashikant Chandekar, senior inspector of Vashi police station, said, "The murder victim was identified as Sujan Kumar Mahato, a resident of Sector 19, Koparkhairane. A passing pedestrian spotted him lying unconscious in a pool of blood on the pavement around 4am. The pedestrian alerted Vashi police station, and our police team reached the spot and took the teenager to NMMC Hospital in Vashi, where he was declared brought dead due to severe blood loss from grievous injuries to his head and wrist after being assaulted with some sharp lethal weapon. The victim Mahato hails from Bihar and resided with his father, who is an auto-rickshaw driver, his mother and two minor siblings. He worked at a roadside Chinese food stall in Koparkhairane and used to drive his father's auto-rickshaw during the night."Inspector Chandekar added, "Mahato had left home on Friday around 9pm, telling his mother that he was going to work at the Chinese food stall and was taking his father's auto-rickshaw to ferry passengers throughout the night.After his body was found early on Saturday morning, his family was informed. His father's auto-rickshaw was not found at the crime scene. Hence, it is suspected that after fatally assaulting Mahato, the assailant took away the auto-rickshaw, which is being traced by scanning CCTV footage along the route from Koparkhairane to Vashi."As there is no CCTV camera surveillance near the crime scene, we are scanning CCTV footage from roads leading to the crime spot where Mahato's body was dumped to zero in on the suspect. Mahato might have been fatally assaulted at the spot, or he might have been assaulted at another location and his body brought in a vehicle and dumped near Mini Seashore. Accordingly, using technical expertise, efforts are being made to detect the murder case. Meanwhile, Mahato's kin and friends are being questioned to get some lead on the unidentified accused."
Article Summary: A 19-year-old man was found murdered near a public garden in Vashi. The Vashi police have registered a murder case against unidentified accused. The victim was identified as Sujan Kumar Mahato, a resident of Sector 19, Koparkhairane.

The rescued youths aged 22-25 years were identified as Om Khilari, Parth Kadve and Rushil Vrindavan.





NAVI MUMBAI: Three youths from Kamothe who went trekking to Chanderi Fort near Panvel lost their way and got stranded before being rescued by the Panvel Taluka Police on Sunday.Gajanan Ghadge, Senior Inspector of Panvel Taluka Police Station, said that the rescued youths, aged between 22 and 25 years, were identified as Om Khilari, Parth Kadve and Rushil Vrindavan. They had started their trek at around 8 am.At around 11 am, the police helpline number 112 received a distress call from one of the trekkers, informing officials that they had lost their way while trekking towards Chanderi Fort."Upon receiving the information, we contacted the caller and asked him to share his live Google location. Accordingly, our police team, along with the Wavanje check-post beat marshal, Ritghar village head Deepak Patil, and the rescue team of NGO Sahyadri Pratishthan, launched a search operation by tracking the youth's mobile location," Ghadge said.The three youths were located within an hour in the hilly terrain and were safely brought down to the foothills.
Article Summary: Three youths from Kamothe who went trekking to Chanderi Fort near Panvel lost their way. They were rescued by the Panvel Taluka Police on Sunday. The youths were located within an hour in the hilly terrain and were safely brought down to the foothills.

Article Title: Navi Mumbai road rage: Ola driver attacked with stick, dragged 2km on car bonnet
Article Text:
The incident occured on the stretch of Sarsole village road in sector 20 near Nerul pond on Aug 15 around 9.35pm.





NAVI MUMBAI: In a road rage incident in Nerul after an argument between the drivers of an Ola cab and a Swift car as the latter claimed that the Ola cab driver had dangerously cut his way while overtaking on the internal road in Nerul on August 15 night, the Swift car driver assaulted the cab driver by punching on his nose and hitting on the head with a bamboo stick causing him severe injuries.As the cab driver bled profusely and attempted to stop the car driver from getting away till the cops arrived, by lying on the car's bonnet, the car driver drove with the cab driver on the bonnet for about 2 kms.The cab driver while recording the incident on his mobile in one hand and firmly holding the bonnet by other hand, shouted for help from passing motorists, while dangling dangerously and requesting the car driver to stop by yelling that he could fall and get killed.As the car slowed down after some distance, the cab driver jumped off the bonnet after which the car driver sped away leaving the cab driver injured on the road.The incident occured on the stretch in sector 20 near Nerul pond on August 15 around 9.35pm.Ajay Kamble, senior inspector of Nerul said, "As per the complaint by the injured cab driver identified as Pradeepkumar Pandey, 27, a resident of Naigaon (E), an FIR was registered at Nerul police station against the unidentified accused car driver, who is absconding.From the Swift car's registration number provided by the complainant, the accused driver was identified as Lalit Arjun Patil, a resident of Juinagar. ""We have invoked relevant BNS sections for the offences of voluntarily causing hurt/ grievous hurt using dangerous weapons or means, voluntarily causing simple hurt, rash or negligent driving on a public way in a manner that endangers human life or is likely to cause hurt or injury to any person and causing simple hurt to any person through a rash or negligent act that endangers human life or personal safety," inspector Kamble added.As per the FIR, on August 15 at 8.18pm, the complainant Pandey had picked up two women passengers from Andheri and dropped them at Seawoods Grand Central mall in Nerul at around 9.30pm.Thereafter, he headed towards Sarsole to attend birthday party of his cousin Nitin Pandey's brother-in-law Rahul Chaubey.Around 9.35pm, when he reached near Nerul pond in sector 20, suddenly a Swift car driver was repeatedly honking. Hence, he changed the lane and gave him way to go ahead.But, the car driver waylaid him and alighting from his car claimed that he had dangerously cut his way while overtaking and punched on his nose, while hurling expletives.As the complainant tried to convince him and told not to give bad words, the car driver went to his vehicle and taking out a bamboo stick, hit on his head causing severe bleeding.As the assailant sat in his car, the complainant tried to stop him, but he started his car. Hence, the complainant lied on the car's bonnet to prevent him from escaping till the cops arrived.The assailant drove with the complainant on the bonnet for about 2kms, reluctant to stop the car.After some distance, as the car slowed down, he jumped off the bonnet and the assailant sped away.The complainant returned to his cab and called his cousin Dipanshu Pandey, who took him to NMMC's Meenatai Thackeray hospital, Nerul.The doctors gave him first aid and for further treatment referred him to NMMC hospital in Vashi, where he was administered sutures to head injury, followed by CT scan.Thereafter, he lodged a police complaint.
Article Summary: The incident occured on the stretch of Sarsole village road in sector 20 near Nerul pond on Aug 15 around 9.35pm. The Swift car driver assaulted the cab driver by punching on his nose and hitting on the head with a bamboo stick causing him severe injuries. The cab driver attempted to stop the car driver from getting away till the cops arrived, by lying on the car's bonnet.

Article Title: 9km uphill, a blazing sun: Runners in Satara tested by an unusually hot day
Article Text:
As many as 7,709 runners crossed the finish line on Sunday of the 21.1-km Satara Hill Half Marathon, widely regarded as one of the toughest races in the country

Pune:





All marathons test physical endurance and mental toughness, but the 21.1-km Satara Hill Half Marathon has one punishing twist: almost immediately after the start, runners find themselves on a nine-kilometre uphill route, leading up to the beautiful Kaas plateau. This means every participant is battling extreme fatigue, even before the halfway mark.“Once that climb starts, is when you realise how demanding this race really is,” said a runner from Pune. “Your breathing becomes heavier, your legs stiffen up, but you keep telling yourself to continue.”Another participant said: “One starts to think about the finish line during the final two kilometres. You can’t do that in this race; you must conserve energy. The mind’s saying ‘run faster’, but the body’s pleading for you to ‘stop’.”As many as 7,709 runners pushed themselves to their limits on Sunday, finishing what is widely regarded as one of the toughest half marathons in the country. More than 180 participants dropped out midway. The event even has a category for runners over 75 years of age; several of them completed the course in under four hours.A major hurdle this year was the weather. Marathon organisers said the event usually sees some light showers and clouds, but on Sunday, the sun was blazing.About 2,000 volunteers were deployed along the route with hydration points at regular intervals. Organisers also set up a 20-bed ICU facility, brought in nearly 100 physiotherapists from medical colleges in Satara and Karad and had eight cardiac ambulances on standby.“We had record registration this year, so extra precautions were taken to ensure the safety of runners. It was indeed sunny this year during the race,” said Vishal Dhane, vice-president of Satara Hill Half Marathon, which is now in its 15th year.Participants came from across the country; there were four foreign nationals too. Organisers said several hotels in Satara city were fully booked for the event.District collector Santosh Patil, who flagged off the race, said the event has become an integral part of the city’s culture. “It’s also along a stunningly beautiful route. We will do everything we can to see this event is on everyone’s calendars for years to come,” Patil said.Santosh Kadam, a teacher from Ambajogai in Beed who crossed the finish line in less than two hours, said it felt like a “momentous achievement”. He’s run the race three times before. “And Sunday was the first time I finished in less than two hours. I’m delighted,” Kadam told TOI after the race.
Article Summary: As many as 7,709 runners crossed the finish line on Sunday of the 21.1-km Satara Hill Half Marathon. The race is widely regarded as one of the toughest half marathons in the country. More than 180 participants dropped out midway.
